\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تطور} (taṭawwara)}{تطور (taṭawwara)}]{\ar{تطور} (taṭawwara) — to evolve}

\label{lesson:AR-C413-tatawwara}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to reduce, then the Arabic for a proportion.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تطور}}
\textbf{\ar{تطور}} — \emph{taṭawwara} — \textquotedblleft{}to evolve\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تطورت} \ar{المدينة} \ar{كثيرا}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{taṭawwarat al-madīna kathīran.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The city has evolved a lot.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتطور}, \emph{yataṭawwar}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تطور}} (\emph{taṭawwara}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ṭ-w-r}, \textquotedblleft{}a time, a stage\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form V, to pass from stage to stage: to evolve.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taṭawwara}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taṭawwara}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taṭawwarat al-madīna kathīran.} — The city has evolved a lot.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to reduce, then the Arabic for a proportion, then say \emph{taṭawwara} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{تطور} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To evolve\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{نما} (namā)}{نما (namā)}]{\ar{نما} (namā) — to grow}

\label{lesson:AR-C413-nama-grow}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a proportion, then the Arabic for to evolve.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{نما}}
\textbf{\ar{نما}} — \emph{namā} — \textquotedblleft{}to grow\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{نما} \ar{الاقتصاد} \ar{هذه} \ar{السنة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{namā al-iqtiṣād hādhihi as-sana.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The economy grew this year.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{ينمو}, \emph{yanmū}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{نما}} (\emph{namā}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{n-m-w}, usually traced to the sense \textquotedblleft{}to grow, to increase\textquotedblright{}. \emph{Namā} is a Form I verb with a weak last letter: to grow. Its present is \emph{yanmū}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تفاقم} (tafāqama)}{تفاقم (tafāqama)}]{\ar{تفاقم} (tafāqama) — to worsen}

\label{lesson:AR-C413-tafaqama}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to evolve, then the Arabic for to grow.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تفاقم}}
\textbf{\ar{تفاقم}} — \emph{tafāqama} — \textquotedblleft{}to worsen\textquotedblright{}.

\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتفاقم}, \emph{yatafāqam}.

\textbf{\ar{تفاقم}} (\emph{tafāqama}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{f-q-m}, \textquotedblleft{}to be full\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form VI, to swell up more and more: to worsen, to grow serious.
\end{cousinweb}

\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{دام} (dāma)}{دام (dāma)}]{\ar{دام} (dāma) — to endure; to last}

\label{lesson:AR-C413-dama}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to worsen, then the Arabic for to recur.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{دام}}
\textbf{\ar{دام}} — \emph{dāma} — \textquotedblleft{}to endure; to last\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{دامت} \ar{الحفلة} \ar{حتى} \ar{منتصف} \ar{الليل}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dāmat al-ḥafla ḥattā muntaṣaf al-layl.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The party lasted until midnight.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يدوم}, \emph{yadūm}.

\ar{ما} \ar{دام}, \emph{mā dāma}, as long as.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{دام}} (\emph{dāma}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{d-w-m}, \textquotedblleft{}to last, to continue\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Dāma} is a Form I verb: to endure, to last. Its present is \emph{yadūm}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[(dialogue)]{Words from chapters 406–413 — a review}

\label{lesson:AR-R413-review-406-413}



\begin{quote}
Say the Arabic for to require and to be available.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item to require, to be available, to suffice, to lack, a procedure
  \item to prove impossible, to entail, to avoid, to avert, to arise unexpectedly
  \item to benefit, to enjoy a right, to deprive, well-being, care
  \item a law, legislation, a clause, to stipulate in writing, to legislate
  \item to permit, to make obligatory, to break a rule, to comply, to exempt
  \item to authorize, to be subject to, to wrong, to struggle against, to approve formally
  \item to become greater, to shrink, to double, to reduce, a proportion
  \item to evolve, to grow, to worsen, to recur, to endure
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
To require? (\textbf{\ar{تطلب}}, \emph{taṭallaba}.) To be available? (\textbf{\ar{توفر}}, \emph{tawaffara}.) To suffice? (\textbf{\ar{كفى}}, \emph{kafā}.) To lack? (\textbf{\ar{افتقر}}, \emph{iftaqara}.) A procedure? (\textbf{\ar{إجراء}}, \emph{ijrāʾ}.) To prove impossible? (\textbf{\ar{تعذر}}, \emph{taʿadhdhara}.) To entail? (\textbf{\ar{استلزم}}, \emph{istalzama}.) To avoid? (\textbf{\ar{تجنب}}, \emph{tajannaba}.) To avert? (\textbf{\ar{تفادى}}, \emph{tafādā}.) To arise unexpectedly? (\textbf{\ar{طرأ}}, \emph{ṭaraʾa}.) To benefit? (\textbf{\ar{استفاد}}, \emph{istafāda}.) To enjoy a right? (\textbf{\ar{تمتع}}, \emph{tamattaʿa}.) To deprive? (\textbf{\ar{حرم}}, \emph{ḥarama}.) Well-being? (\textbf{\ar{رفاهية}}, \emph{rafāhiyya}.) Care? (\textbf{\ar{رعاية}}, \emph{riʿāya}.) A law? (\textbf{\ar{قانون}}, \emph{qānūn}.) Legislation? (\textbf{\ar{تشريع}}, \emph{tashrīʿ}.) A clause? (\textbf{\ar{بند}}, \emph{band}.) To stipulate in writing? (\textbf{\ar{نص}}, \emph{naṣṣa}.) To legislate? (\textbf{\ar{شرع}}, \emph{sharraʿa}.) To permit? (\textbf{\ar{أباح}}, \emph{abāḥa}.) To make obligatory? (\textbf{\ar{أوجب}}, \emph{awjaba}.) To break a rule? (\textbf{\ar{خالف}}, \emph{khālafa}.) To comply? (\textbf{\ar{التزم}}, \emph{iltazama}.) To exempt? (\textbf{\ar{أعفى}}, \emph{aʿfā}.) To authorize? (\textbf{\ar{أجاز}}, \emph{ajāza}.) To be subject to? (\textbf{\ar{خضع}}, \emph{khaḍaʿa}.) To wrong? (\textbf{\ar{ظلم}}, \emph{ẓalama}.) To struggle against? (\textbf{\ar{كافح}}, \emph{kāfaḥa}.) To approve formally? (\textbf{\ar{أقر}}, \emph{aqarra}.) To become greater? (\textbf{\ar{ازداد}}, \emph{izdāda}.) To shrink? (\textbf{\ar{تقلص}}, \emph{taqallaṣa}.) To double? (\textbf{\ar{تضاعف}}, \emph{taḍāʿafa}.) To reduce? (\textbf{\ar{قلل}}, \emph{qallala}.) A proportion? (\textbf{\ar{نسبة}}, \emph{nisba}.) To evolve? (\textbf{\ar{تطور}}, \emph{taṭawwara}.) To grow? (\textbf{\ar{نما}}, \emph{namā}.) To worsen? (\textbf{\ar{تفاقم}}, \emph{tafāqama}.) To recur? (\textbf{\ar{تكرر}}, \emph{takarrara}.) To endure? (\textbf{\ar{دام}}, \emph{dāma}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
